Subject: Production latency + 5xx spike (US-west)

Olga —

We started seeing a latency increase around 07:50 PST and now ~18% of requests are returning 5xx. Throughput is also throttled on our side (timeouts at 3s). This is impacting our customer-facing inference path. Can you confirm if this is on Redwood's side or if this is an integration/config change? We need an ETA and an interim mitigation (re-route, throttling, anything).

Attached: trace_log_20260318.zip (filtered request traces)

—Sean
Head of Platform
BrightBridge Analytics
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, logan_wright@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Production latency + 5xx spike (US-west) — urgent triage

Team —

Just received the note from BrightBridge. They report ~18% 5xx and elevated p95 latency. This is their production customer-facing route (high volume, pinned to dedicated pool). We need:
- Immediate confirmation of control-plane events or autoscaler activity (Logan)
- Kernel/runtime probe for GPU saturations & memory pressure (Marcus)
- Quick mitigation options (model fallback, reduced concurrency, soft-quotas) with customer-facing ETA (Marissa)

I will loop back to Sean within 30 minutes with an interim status and a 2-hour remediation ETA. Please mark any artifacts/attachments you produce with the run id.

This thread must remain within leadership/sales/ops (no external comms besides the update I'll send).

—Olga Petrov
Chief Revenue Officer (interim)
Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, logan_wright@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 08:38:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Production latency + 5xx spike (US-west) — quick findings

Quick summary from runtime side:
- No recent deploys to that dedicated pool. No control-plane maintenance windows.
- Observed sustained GPU utilization >96% on two nodes in pool-dedicated-west-02 starting 07:48 PST.
- KV cache miss rates spiked concurrently (likely invalidation storm from a cold prefix flush).
- Error signatures show OOM-retries on CUDA inference worker leading to transient 5xx.

Immediate actions I recommend (in order):
1) Drop concurrency on pool-dedicated-west-02 to 30% of current to reduce OOM churn (expected p95 improvement but throughput reduction).
2) Enable fallback routing to quantized LLM-qa-2q for non-critical routes (compatible but slightly lower quality).
3) Evict affected nodes and re-provision from warm spare to clear kernel fragmentation.

I'll attach heap/tracer snippets in ~10m. If we need faster latency, we can also temporarily route a subset of traffic to eu-west if customer agrees to cross-region.

—Marcus Lin
VP, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: logan_wright@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Production latency + 5xx spike (US-west) — runbook output

Runbook output (run id: rb-20260318-01):
- Autoscaler: no scale-up events; quota saturation hit on pool (concurrency cap).
- Node health: two nodes reporting CUDA OOM and kernel restart loops; drained 3 lower-util nodes prematurely.
- Network: no inter-region networking errors.
- Logs attached: stability_playback-08-12.txt (2MB text, sample traces)

Proposed immediate mitigation:
- Authorize me to apply policy: reduce concurrency to 30% on pool-dedicated-west-02 and enable fallback route for 40% of requests to model-llm-qa-2q.
- If authorized, I will also schedule a rolling replacement of the two faulty nodes (expected 12–18 min).

Impact: throughput will drop ~35% while p95 should drop to <700ms for routed traffic.

Please reply ACK if green to proceed.

—Logan Wright
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@brightbridge.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, logan_wright@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency + 5xx spike (US-west) — interim status and next steps

Sean —

Thank you for the traces. Short update and next steps:

What we see:
- Root cause appears to be GPU memory churn in the dedicated pool serving your pinned model. This caused a cascade of OOM retries and transient 5xx.

Immediate mitigations (being applied now):
- We are reducing concurrency on your dedicated pool by 70% to stabilize p95 (expect immediate reduction in errors).
- We will route ~40% of non-critical inference requests to a quantized model variant (slightly lower quality but faster) to preserve responsiveness for high-priority traffic.
- A rolling node replacement is in progress (ETA 15–20 minutes to clear kernel fragmentation).

Customer impact: you should see fewer 5xx and lower p95 for prioritized routes within ~10 minutes. Throughput may be reduced briefly while we stabilize.

We will follow up with a full incident timeline, artifacts, and proposed SLA credit as appropriate.

Attachments: stakeholder_update-20260318.pdf (initial status & remediation plan)

Please let me know if you need us to route traffic to eu-west as a temporary cross-region fallback; that would add ~60–80ms to median latency but may increase success rate if you prefer absolute throughput.

—Olga Petrov
Chief Revenue Officer (interim)
Redwood Inference

1) We will need the filtered traces you referenced and the kernel OOM snippets for our internal postmortem (we attached our traces earlier). Can you upload those to the Drive link?
2) Please document the expected SLA credit calculation and initial estimate. Procurement is copied.

We appreciate the team moving quickly. Please keep this as our primary channel for updates.

—Sean
